Port's clear — iteration 9 loads on open, and your **"Search tips"** link is now beside the search box (click it any time). Now let's look at the **edges** together. These demo links show view-only states so you can see how things hold up.

---

**1. When there's nothing there (new library / empty views)**
Open **[http://maker:4001/?demo=empty](http://maker:4001/?demo=empty)**. This is what a brand-new library looks like — *"Your library is empty. Paste a link above to add something."* Click across **Unread** ("all caught up") and **Archived** ("Nothing archived"). Do these calm empty messages feel welcoming and clear?

**2. Very long content**
Open **[http://maker:4001/?demo=long](http://maker:4001/?demo=long)**. One entry has an over-long title, a long description, seven tags, and a long formatted note. Right now **titles shorten with an ellipsis** and **descriptions clamp to two lines**, while your **note shows in full**. Does that balance feel right — keep long titles/descriptions trimmed for a calm list, with the full text available on Edit? Or would you rather see the whole title?

**3. A large library (hundreds of links)**
Open **[http://maker:4001/?demo=many](http://maker:4001/?demo=many)** — 300 links. Notice the tab counts, and that search/tags still narrow instantly (try the search box). It's currently **one continuous list**. As your library grows into the hundreds or thousands, would you want it to stay a single long scroll, or start **loading in pages / "load more"** so the screen stays light? (This is the one open design question here.)

**4. When a save goes wrong** (back on the normal library — **[http://maker:4001](http://maker:4001)**)
- Type something that isn't a real address (e.g. `just some words`) and press **Save** — you get a clear message instead of a silent failure.
- Save a real-looking but unreachable address, e.g. `https://no-such-site-xyz-123.example` — the details can't be read, so the **review panel still opens and invites you to fill in the title/description yourself**, rather than losing the save. Does handling an unreadable page that way match what you'd want?

One more, in words rather than a screen: entries show **relative times** ("just now", "3 h ago", "2 d ago"). For older links, would you prefer that switch to an actual date (e.g. "23 Sep")? 

Tell me how these edges feel, and your call on the large-library question — then I'll have what I need to propose building the real thing.
